column3: The Hebrew says “they slaughtered the Passover”; BSB uses the passive and explicitly supplies “lamb.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed here and says “the house”; BSB names Josiah and says “the temple.”
The Hebrew separately mentions the writing of David and the writing of Solomon; BSB combines them as instructions written by both.
The Hebrew says “the Passover” and “your brothers”; BSB supplies “lambs” and says “your fellow countrymen.”
The Hebrew says the animals came from the possessions of the king; BSB specifies his own flocks and herds.
The Hebrew leaves the blood and the skinned animals unexpressed as objects; BSB explicitly supplies them.
The Hebrew repeats “gate and gate” and says “their brothers, the Levites”; BSB says “each gate” and “their fellow Levites.”
The Hebrew says “the house”; BSB says “the temple.”
The Hebrew leaves the sender unnamed here; BSB names Neco.
The Hebrew says he died and was buried, then repeats the name Josiah as the object of mourning; BSB names Josiah at burial and uses “him” for the mourning.
The Hebrew says male and female singers; BSB says choirs of men and women. The Hebrew says the laments are written “in the laments”; BSB explicitly calls it the Book of Laments.
